Heated Gloves, Rechargeable Heating Gloves, Winter Touchscreen Warm Gloves for Women and Men, Waterproof Touchscreen USB Heating Gloves for Motorcycle Fishing Hiking Cycling Skiing in order for these to work, you will need some kind of battery pack/portable charger (BOUGHT SEPERATELY of course which ISN'T advertised) And you will have to run these annoying wires through whatever coat you are wearing from arm to arm, and deal with having wires throughout your clothes. You would be better off just getting the ones that use regular built in battery packs.

The fit is nice enough I suppose (given that I have tiny hands). I was expecting them to be too big as they were advertised as adult gloves, but they actually fit quite well. So if you have normal adult sized hands, these may be a bit small for you. They only seem to have heat on the outside of the glove, so I don't know how well these will work for their intended use (for keeping my hands warm while biking this winter) But I guess we will see.

They take quite a while before you start feeling heat too, so you may want to put these on about 5 minutes or so before you head out into the cold. Over all, I guess they are ok... but their having advertising them as "rechargeable" is rather annoying because it leads the buyer to assume they come with some kind of rechargeable battery pack. THEY DO NOT! So you better have a portable charger handy or you will have wasted your money.
text_fidelity_b: Heated Gloves, Rechargeable Heating Gloves, Winter Touchscreen Warm Gloves for Women and Men, Waterproof Touchscreen USB Heating Gloves for Motorcycle Fishing Hiking Cycling Skiing

CAT EYE, Strada Cadence Wired Bike Computer For the past two or three years I have used a cheap Bell F20 bicycle computer. While it functioned, I found that installation was a hassle, programming was awkward at best, and placement was limited to the front wheel. However, it was cheap.

This product is light-years ahead of the cheapy models while maintaining a median pricing position. Installation is not difficult but was time consuming for me. Coordinating the placement of sensors and magnets was finicky on my Trek FX. The unit is designed to accomodate the rear wheel of the bike which I like for when I am on the trainer.

Programming was again not difficult but laborious and similar in nature to that of the Bell F20. Once programmed it is easy to cyle through modes and understand what is going on.

Others have noted that the screen is smaller than expected. I was also surprised at the diminutive size of the computer, but information is legible to me. Nonetheless, if glasses are a must then they should be worn.

I like this computer and would recommend it to anyone. It is a nice intermediate model that installs pretty easily, works reliably, and has an intuitive interface.
text_fidelity_b: CAT EYE, Strada Cadence Wired Bike Computer

Universal UB300 Adjustable Bench (Discontinued) This is the perfect bench for a home gym. It has all of the incline levels I need to do my workouts. I like how it also has a -10 degree incline for situps, etc.
The material covering the bench is high quality and has held up to workouts easily. It is also easy to clean in between workouts. Changing the incline is straight-forward and due to the simplicity in the design it will hold up longer than other benches with a more complicated incline selection mechanism. One thing that is a bit annoying about this bench are the foot pegs. The round plastic side pieces that keep the pads on will pop out very easily. Any real use will pop them out and I guarantee within a week or two those plastic pieces will be lost.

Dimensions are confirmed as advertised.

Pros:
*Easy to select incline
*Durable
*Easy to clean

Cons:
*Side plastic pieces on foot pegs easily pop out(-1/2 a star)

Additional Considerations:
Make sure you purchase the proper weights and other safety equipment to go along with this bench. If you are bench pressing, get a power rack and do not bench without a spotter.

Overall: 4.5/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 5 stars

If you have any further questions regarding the product in my review please leave a comment below and I will get back to you as soon as possible.

I trust the charging circuitry on an Energizer-branded flashlight more than on a generic flashlight (and the batteries in these flashlights are powerful enough that safe recharging is important). The flashlight has 3 brightness modes plus one flashing mode. I like that the strobe mode needs to be activated by a double-tap on the power button, so I am very unlikely to get that mode accidentally (and I hate flashlights that start strobing when I don't want them to). The steady mode has a nice wide uniform beam despite the flashlight having a compact size (1.2 inches at the widest). A lot of cheaper flashlights are bright only in the center, then fade rapidly towards the sides. I find the uniform beam to be much more useful.

Yes, the battery is not replaceable and the whole unit will have to be discarded when the battery no longer holds it charge. Hopefully that will be after hundreds of charges, which is many years for me and I'll probably lose the flashlight before that happens. If you use your flashlight for hours every day, then this may be a bigger concern to you.

text_fidelity_a:
Travel Kuppe Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Cycling Sports Water Bottle, Includes Both Straw and Sip Lid If you must have a steel water bottle on your bicycle (for health or other reasons), this may be for you. However, there are many disadvantages. First, this bottle is big - about 1 inch taller than a 24 ounce plastic water bottle, even though the capacity is a smaller 20 ounces. Of course, this bottle is less efficient with space because of the insulation feature. The extra height will cause problems with smaller bicycles, especially in the seat tube water bottle cage. While the straw cap seems interesting, in practice this is useless on a bicycle. With the straw open, the bottle will not fit on my bicycle. With the straw closed, you need 2 hands to open the straw, which is dangerous while riding your bicycle. There are plastic insulated bicycle water bottles on the market that are much cheaper and lighter weight than this (eg Polar or Camelbak) and they don't need the straw since you can just squeeze them to squirt the water out.

This bottle is also very heavy - 11.5 ounces compared to 3 ounces for a standard plastic water bottle. Gripping this bottle is much more difficult than a plastic bottle since (1) it is slippery when wet and (2) it doesn't squeeze when gripped like a plastic bottle. I do not recommend using this bottle with metal water bottle cages since it rattles like crazy; a plastic water bottle cage may be better, especially if it has a grippy interior.

The insulation does work, but you only have 20 ounces of water in there so if you drink that in the first hour of your ride, can you refill the bottle with more cold water or just with tap water that isn't cold enough to be worth insulating? If you're not drinking at least 20 ounces per hour on a day that is hot enough to need an insulated water bottle, you are not drinking enough to avoid dehydration.

As a bicycle water bottle, I give this only 2 stars because of all the limitations. For use in a car's cup holder or similar it may work better, but then you're competing with dozens of other steel water bottles that cost much less, so I give it 2 stars for that use case as well.
text_fidelity_b: Travel Kuppe Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Cycling Sports Water Bottle, Includes Both Straw and Sip Lid

text_fidelity_a:
Sawyer Products SP2129 Micro Squeeze Water Filtration System, 1 Pack, Black/Blue One thing you don't want to scrimp on is water filtering when you're hiking. Sawyer has an excellent reputation in the field, and we've used a different Sawyer filter for two years quite happily. This is a nice addition to their line-up.

Pros:
Size: it's small, compact, and quite light

Easy to use: screw it on to the included 32 0z. bladder once you've filled it, onto most regular types of disposable plastic water bottles (but please don't use those!), onto many bladders, or use the included straw to drink from the water source directly (though less comfortably). That's it.

Water flow: It comes out quickly enough to drink directly without any annoying pause or lag (you can also squeeze the bag for more flow).

Drinking bag feels quite durable, always a concern for these sorts of filters. I wouldn't be worried about this one.

Comes with an extra gasket, straw, and cleaning syringe

Backflushing is easy and quick

Quasi-negatives
Doesn't do viruses. I don't consider this a real negative since a) if you're hiking in the US you don't need to worry about viruses and b) if you're looking for something to take care of viruses you're looking for a real step up in price and product so that's a whole different category

No instructions. This is more just a little annoying, but easily solved by going online and looking at the videos.

It's a great little product from a trustworthy source. Water filters have come a long way from the old bulky pump action and so if you're still using one of those, consider moving up to something like this. So much easier and better to carry.
text_fidelity_b: Sawyer Products SP2129 Micro Squeeze Water Filtration System, 1 Pack, Black/Blue

Tents for Camping: Sportneer Tent for 2/3 Persons Family Pop Up Instant Tents Waterproof with Removable Top Rainfly Easy Set Up Tent 94.5"x86.6"x59" [[VIDEOID:64c8658b81382127e4a89d8e490ca985]] My kids love camping, so when we got this tent they were excited to try popping it up in our playroom first before we take it out. Before I go any further, I want to point out that to its' credit, this tent was easy enough for a couple of girls aged 9 and 11 to figure it out themselves.
That being said, I'm glad we did it at home first because I noticed at least one weird design flaw: The outer door cover is REALLY difficult to close from the inside. You see, like many tents, the doors are two layers: an outer rain flap and an inner bug-net window screen. bug net opens in the middle with a zipper, and the outer later opens on the sides (attached from the top, zipper around the perimeter).
This is odd because it seems like it is only designed to be closed from the outside like this! The zipper for the outer flap has an inside handle, but if the bug screen is closed, you can't reach it. I suppose you could open the bug screen all the way in order to get to the zipper, but it seems a whole lot easier to close and open both from the outside than the inside, which I wasn't expecting.
I'm not sure how I feel about that, I suppose it will still do the job out at a campsite, but it just feels poorly thought out.
text_fidelity_b: Tents for Camping: Sportneer Tent for 2/3 Persons Family Pop Up Instant Tents Waterproof with Removable Top Rainfly Easy Set Up Tent 94.5"x86.6"x59"

Kootek LED Safety Light Red Flashing with Free Clip on Straps Sport Running Warning Strobe Tail Lights for Dog Collar, Walking, Cycling, Bike, Helmet, Batteries Included [2 Pack] I received these as a free review sample. Others have covered the myriad of uses, so I will confine my review to some features that I like and other aspects that I tested.

One of the nicest features is the fact that you can clip this on to a belt loop, shirt of even a helmet (using the short strips of velcro and some glue). As I was testing these I did notice that while the clip is convenient, it may be TOO convenient. It's so easy to attach to a piece of apparel that you may wind up clipping it to a pocket that obscures it if you are wearing a loose over shirt. That is not a flaw in the design as much as my giving a head's up that how you use it is important.

The light is not super bright (nor should it be since you do not want to distract drivers), so if you absolutely want to be seen the flash mode is perfect on dark, unlit streets and roads. Also, for biking or walking I recommend using both lights - one in the back and one in the front of your person - so that you can be seen from both directions.

While the product specs do not claim this is waterproof I did submerge one of the lights in a sink of water for two minutes and it remained operational. It may not be actually waterproof, but will not fail in inclement weather.

Overall, this is a great way to remain safe on foot or bike, and the lights are nicely built.
text_fidelity_b: Kootek LED Safety Light Red Flashing with Free Clip on Straps Sport Running Warning Strobe Tail Lights for Dog Collar, Walking, Cycling, Bike, Helmet, Batteries Included [2 Pack]

text_fidelity_a:
Gonex Hand Crank Collapsible Outdoor LED Camping Lantern USB Rechargeable Mini Flashlight Hiking Torch light lamp Camp lanterns serve a couple of useful purposes. They can help light an area when outdoors (and camping) and they can be used as an emergency light source when there is need for extra light (such as during a power outage). Battery-powered lanterns offer more convenience and do not require liquid fuels. This particular lantern is especially suited for emergencies as it has a rechargeable power supply and it also has a hand-crank for getting short bursts of emergency power when it is otherwise depleted.

This is a small lantern that is a little smaller in diameter than a typical coaster. It is bright orange which will make it easy to find, even on a cluttered desk in the daylight. It is a collapsible unit and when collapsed (as it comes in the package) it is less than 2” thick and when expanded is about 5” tall.

It has two brightness modes, one being somewhat bright and the other being very bright. On the bottom of this lantern is a lens that sits over the internal LED and when the lantern is expanded the lens lets through a well-diffused and gentle light that illuminates a wide area. When collapsed the light coming from the lens is much more concentrated and is bright and defined enough to serve as a flashlight.

The power source for this lantern is an internal rechargeable battery. This can be charged with the included cable, but it is not a USB cable and instead uses a round plug. This is the one criticism I have of this lantern – don’t lose that cable. But…in addition to the cable the lantern includes a crank mechanism that can deliver some emergency power to the battery when needed, requiring a little manual effort. Unless you want to crank for a long, long time, do not expect the crank to charge this lantern up all the way or even close to it. It’s there for emergencies, not a primary charging source.

The unit is fairly rugged and weatherproof. It is sealed up nicely and should hold up well in adverse weather like light rain. I would not try to submerge it but I suspect it would survive if dropped in water briefly.

I like this lantern and I can see the possibilities with it. It’s a great little emergency light and it can work as a flashlight or a lantern. It’s small and it packs well. Just don’t lose the charging cable.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: Gonex Hand Crank Collapsible Outdoor LED Camping Lantern USB Rechargeable Mini Flashlight Hiking Torch light lamp

Premium Pickleball Carry Bag for Multiple Paddles Set Holder Backpack Pack with Convenient Pockets for Phone, Keys, Wallet… I have been wanting to play pickle ball again for a long time. As a GenXer I grew up playing in high school gym and actually enjoyed it. It took some talking my wife into. But I started by grabbing a pickle ball set from this same company. The bag and set arrived yesterday and today at lunch we went out... our apartment community has a tennis court, but according to our online research, you can at least get started, but know the tennis court net and lines are not exact. No worries, it was a blast! By halfway through lunch my wife was talking about getting back out there tomorrow.

The set is excellent (look for that review) and we found that both paddles and a ball fit perfectly. We actually had 3 balls in there as well as using the little pocket to store my keys in. I’m going to get a carabiner to hook it to the fence while today I had it hooked over the net pole.

The bag is simple and basic. I would say the quality is average. Yes, there are much nicer bags out there and we would/will consider one if we get to the point of playing often and getting into a higher level. But for now this bag and set work perfectly and we are absolutely happy with the purchase.

The bag is net so it can breath and won’t retain smells. There is enough room for 2 paddles and 3 balls, though the instructions say there are a combination of options: 3 paddle and 1-2 balls or 1 paddle and more balls. But for our needs (2/3) it is perfect. The smaller pocket is in fact small, but my keys fit fine. You could not likely fit a wallet or more than a set or two of keys.

It is light weight, which was fine for walking to and from the courts - 1/4 mile - and carrying it over my shoulder going and in my hand by the handle coming back. The strap for the shoulder is adjustable.

We are most certainly happy and are pleased with this purchase. We look forward to many more days playing and getting back into great shape.

Hydracentials Insulated Stainless Steel Metal Water Bottle with Straw Lid - Vacuum Insulated Water Bottles, Keeps Hot and Cold - Sports Canteen Bottle This is the smaller version of the second generation bottle. More about that in a minute. The reasons why I love this are the smaller size that fits in the beverage holder in my vehicle, and the improvements that were made when the second generation was released.

Improvements include the double wall construction that not only keeps this one (and the [[ASIN:B00LFPS0CY Hydracentials Sporty 25 Oz]] sibling) from sweating, but provides the insulation to keep drinks colder longer.

I can attest that the eight hour claim is absolutely true. To be sure it does not keep it ice cold that long, but it sure keeps it cold. I left mine in my car - with the insulation sock that shipped with mine - and it was cold hours later. This was in 95 degree weather, which would have turned a regular bottle of water hot. I am serious about that/ I did not test this without the additional insulating sock, but I am guessing that the water would have not gotten any warmer than cool without it.

Mine also came with a pair of straw cleaning brushes. I have not used those yet because I have found that soaking the top, straw and bottle in hot, soapy water, rinsing with a jet of clear water and air drying work perfectly.

Do note that this is NOT for hot liquids. It was not designed for them, and a hot liquid would probably ruin both the straw and the swivel piece to which it connects.

For me this is the ideal size, but click on the link to the 25 ounce model if you like your water supersized. Either way I think you'll be happy with one of these models because they are an improvement over others on the market that I have used, including this brand's original bottle.

It turns on with a long press of the side button. A short press will select high or low heat. (A display of "50" means low heat, "60" means high heat.) After a few seconds of operation, the battery charge is displayed (up to 100). Another long press will turn it off.

It gets very warm, and heats evenly all over, probably because it's aluminum underneath. It has a smooth texture and size and shape that's easy to grip and feels comfortable in hand.

The button switch for the light is on the bottom, where the USB ports are. The light turns on and changes modes with short presses, and can be turned off from any mode with a long press.

It recharges via USB C, and an adapter cable is included (standard USB to USB C). A charger is not included.

This hand warmer can also be used as a battery bank for recharging devices. A USB out port is on the bottom.

A couple of knocks: One is the projector feature. It comes with some colorful cartoony slides that you can place under the translucent light dome. The pictures don't project very well onto the wall or ceiling. They're very blurry and there's no focusing. Mostly they just project onto the light dome itself.

The other is the light diffusing dome. It's easily removed by turning slightly counterclockwise, but it doesn't lock securely back on the device. It seems like it could easily come off in a pocket or purse, and it's needed if you plan to you the light feature, otherwise the LEDs would be shining directly. Since I don't plan to use the projector feature and won't need to remove the dome, I plan to just secure the dome in place with some tape.

Also in the box (and it's a nice box) is a carrying bag, a lanyard, and an instruction sheet with very small print. The box, incidentally, opens by lifting the end up like a flap. It took a few seconds for me to figure that out. Something in the box smelled like eucalyptus. I think it was the carrying pouch. I'm not too fond of fragrances so I won't be using it, but I'm sure it's nice for those who do.
text_fidelity_b: edola Rechargeable Hand Warmers Outdoor, USB Chargeable Portable Small Heated Hand Warmers with Light for Camping, 6000mah Electronic Pocket Heater for Football Golf Gaming

It came with some screws broken loose and slight damage on the underside of the wood. I can't ding it too badly for that, because it still works, and it took a subsequent fall with no real damage. The cat likes to sit on it (usually while we're playing) and it can handle her weight just fine.

It is a little small, and for a serious player this will aid with control more than with those power shots. For a casual player, it's a sufficient experience to be highly entertaining. I'm having a good time with it.

It's a great concept, but it has too many quality issues for it to merit more than three stars.

Stanley The Quadvac Trigger Action Mug, Canvas, 16OZ This is the best thermos I've owned to date, but it's far from perfect.

If you put piping hot coffee in it, it will keep it hot for about 45 minutes, and keep it warm for about 2 more hours after that. I haven't used it for cold drinks.

I love the handle style; that's my favorite part about it. Most handled thermoses have this infuriating issue of the mouthpiece never lining up properly with where the handle is, so you always have to hold them weirdly to drink from them. On this thermos, the handle is fabric, and can be adjusted 360 degrees around the thermos, so no matter where the mouthpiece ends up, you can just adjust the handle to be right where you need it. the other nice thing about the fabric handle is that you won't break it by bumping it into things or dropping it.

The worst part about this thing is cleaning it. The entire head of it is very complex, with lots of moving parts, springs, and plastic bits - ALL of which are submerged in whatever you are drinking. So, when you take the lid off, you have disassemble the whole thing and either soak all the parts, or wash them all individually. Don't be lazy and put off cleaning it until the next day or you'll have whatever you drank caked all though the innards. If you don't mind keeping it clean, it's really nice. I'm very happy with it.
text_fidelity_b: Stanley The Quadvac Trigger Action Mug, Canvas, 16OZ

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Arctic Trails Hiking Poles - Lightweight - Anti Shock Technology - Great for All Skill Levels I've had a set of MSR trek poles for over a decade now. I've used them to travel though the Zion river, down and up the grand canyon, through forests of sequoias and so on. They've always worked well, but there's been newer tech since I first bought them.

So I put them side by side for a comparison. Here's how's the two stack up.
They both operate in the same way as far as extending and turning to lock them.
They are both clearly marked so you always knows your set length.
As shown in the photo, the MSRs are a bit taller when extended. They're both just about the same height when collapsed.
The MSRs did not come with option for swappable end caps.
The hand grips on these are softer.
As shown in the other photo, the tip shield on the MSRs are indexed so they interlock. That keeps them from swinging around.
And probably the biggest difference is that these have shock absorption. There's just enough spring to take off some of the abruptness of planting these down on unstable footing without there being too much travel to throw off stability.

So overall, they work well. They're an improvement overt the old ones in some ways. In others, they're not.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Arctic Trails Hiking Poles - Lightweight - Anti Shock Technology - Great for All Skill Levels

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge 2 Heart Rate + Fitness Wristband, Teal, Small (US Version) My husband purchased this for me for Christmas. I like the tracker, it is a better-looking device than the old Charge HR and does a decent job tracking steps, HR, etc. but has some flaws. HR is relatively accurate, but at times, and only when I am walking versus doing high-intensity workouts, the device will say that my HR is over 180 when my max HR for high-intensity cardio is more like 168. It also tends to under-count my steps, which I think is preferable to over-counting them, but still annoying. Also, it is hard to get my Charge 2 to switch between screens by "tapping it". It normally takes having to tap it really hard to get it to switch screens. Other than that, it gives me a rough estimate for my steps for the day, encourages me to move frequently (with the 250 steps/hr function), and gives me an idea of my HR during various exercises (not super accurate, but I'm only looking for a ballpark estimate/compare my HR across activities).

That said, the biggest physical flaw I'm seeing is with the new band attachment method. When I got my tracker new, I noticed that on one side of the tracker, the band wasn't attaching as tightly as the other. I didn't think much of it at the time, but over the course of five months, it has gotten progressively worse to the point that one side of the band will easily be "bumped" off the tracker and the whole device will detach from my wrist. I notified customer service about the issue and they did send me a new band free of charge, however, it was like pulling teeth to get them to replace a $30 band. I first received an e-mail from CS stating that I needed to take a photo of the problem with my case number present in the photo as well as the FitBit logo on my device, which was no small feat to accomplish given the location of my band's issue. I did take the photo for them (though it took two sets of hands to get everything in the photo the way CS wanted it), but I felt that the process of getting a replacement band was very frustrating and put a lot of ridiculous demands on the consumer to "prove" the problem, only to simply replace a $30 band.

In any case, I recommend the FitBit - it's not a perfect device, and customer service from the company is overly frustrating to fix a problem that's well-known (check the FitBit boards) and cheap for the company to fix without making the customer jump through flaming hoops.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 2 Heart Rate + Fitness Wristband, Teal, Small (US Version)

Although it doesn't get in the way of my shifting or brake cables, I can see a configuration where it would. A more adaptable mounting mechanism may be in order to handle a larger number of bike variants.

My initial response was that I wish it had more light modes but after using it on the streets and trails round Boston I've found 2 that I switch between and I'm happy. The "Steady Pulse" works well for traffic notification. I've watched cars very specifically react to the light at a good distance even though I'm angling it down to not blind too many people. I can also see it flicker on reflective paint on signs so I know it's got good distance. I also use the low setting for dark bike baths so I don't blind oncoming bikers/runners. I can also easily angle it to one side or the other as well to get it out of people's faces.

text_fidelity_a:
ROLA 59721 Removable Anchor Point Xtreme APX Series Roof Rack for Pontiac Vibe, Toyota Matrix Mine came with the anchors assembled correctly (see another review here for this important information!!).

Added to a 2009 Pontiac Vibe GT.

Very happy with these. Easy to attach. I know nothing of cars or mechanical things and instructions were clear & detailed. Instruction pics are accurate and I was never lost following them. It took me about 30-40 minutes to attach to my car.

I have read that crossbars can be noisy so I'll mention that I haven't heard any sound coming from these at all yet. I drove with a 55 pound kayak 1.5 hours on both freeway (I only went 65mph) and highway (55-60). No noise with or without the kayak *with sunroof closed. *With sunroof open I can hear a light whistle at 40mph.

The locks/keys did have to be jiggled a little but not enough to take a star off.

One reviewer mentions that because of the roof slant of Vibe/Matrix, things sit unevenly on bars with objects pointing upward toward the front of the car. I see this too, but it wasn't enough of an angle to be of concern on my car. There are front and back designated bars but I couldn't see any difference in them. I think it would be ideal if ROLA revisited their design to make the back bar an inch taller and just eliminate this issue completely from their product.

Note: the only tool you will need is a 10mm socket wrench. I bought a cheap $3.99 set and don't recommend doing that. The teeth inside the socket stripped and although I did tighten all screws, I bet the last two could have been tighter if the socket hadn't stripped by that point. Not a place you want to 'skimp' - tightening down screws that keep heavy things from flying off your car - so in hindsight I recommend using a decent socket set for this job.

I will update if my experience with these changes over the long term.
text_fidelity_b: ROLA 59721 Removable Anchor Point Xtreme APX Series Roof Rack for Pontiac Vibe, Toyota Matrix

text_fidelity_a:
G4Free 2/4/13 PCS Camping Cookware Mess Kit Hiking Backpacking Picnic Cooking Bowl Non Stick Pot Knife Spoon Set This is a decent set of camping cookware consisting of four pots, each with handles (but no lids). The set nestles together into a pretty compact stack that measures about 7 inches tall and about 5 inches wide. It also comes with a mesh pouch to hold the pots when they are stacked together. It makes for a small, easily toted package.

The build quality is decent but not exceptional. The pans are aluminum and somwhat thin. The metal is thick enough so that the pots won't dent easily, but you can flex the pan if you squeeze them hard. The handles have a silicon coating on them which is nice for helping with heat protection (although you still need a mitt or pad to grab the handle if the pot has been on the fire for a while). The handles fold easily and take up very little room. However, the bracket that attaches the handles to the pot, as well as the handles themselves, are not all that sturdy. They are functional, but won't stand up to much (or any) abuse.

The pot sizes are fine for cooking for one or two people (perhaps you could stretch it to three if everyone is a light eater).

For occasional camping (or the rare emergency) use, these are more than durable enough to get the job done, and do so in a very space-conservative fashion. For that, I'd give them 4-stars. If, however, you're an especially avid camper, or need to cook for more than two people, you'll probably want a larger, more durable set.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: G4Free 2/4/13 PCS Camping Cookware Mess Kit Hiking Backpacking Picnic Cooking Bowl Non Stick Pot Knife Spoon Set

text_fidelity_a:
90 Degree By Reflex High Waist Fleece Lined Leggings with Side Pocket - Yoga Pants First of all, i bought this pants not entirely for yoga and thus i picked the one with pockets. I needed a pair of leggings with fleece that i can walk my dog during winter (in California!!). Don't judge me...but i am terrified of the cold. I bought the pants in two sizes, two colors; all with pockets.

FIT:
"M" and "S" fits me perfectly because the material is super stretchy and extremely comfortable. I'm 5'6 and 133lbs. "M" has the length that would wrap around the heel nicely and it doesn't feel bulky. I ended up taking the "S" simply because it was in black and i didn't want to take the trouble of returning. But on the hindsight, i would have preferred the "M" so i can pull it over my heel and not worry about wearing out the material over time.

COMFORT:
The fleece is very smooth and comfy. Definitely not a thin legging that you can wear underneath a pair of skinny jeans (unfortunately!). The pockets do add on the extra thickness.

WARMTH:
In an evening of ~50F, wearing just the leggings, socks and a pair of running shoes still left my feet feeling cold (again, don't judge the Californians..it's just me!). I couldn't walk my dog comfortably unless i start jogging to build up the heat. When I swapped my running shoes with a pair of Uggs/boots that gave me more coverage, it helped a lot. I've seen reviews where people would wear it outdoor in the snow under some snow pants... i dont know if I can make the same comparison.

Overall, i just love how comfortable the pants are. Not super expensive but also not as cheap.
text_fidelity_b: 90 Degree By Reflex High Waist Fleece Lined Leggings with Side Pocket - Yoga Pants

Sunny Health & Fitness Magnetic Recumbent Exercise Bike with Silent Belt Drive, Performance Monitor, BMI and Body Fat Calculator, 275 LB Max Weight - SF-RB4953 So far, so good! Assembling this exercise bike went pretty smoothly. I didn't have any issues getting through the instructions and had no missing pieces/parts, which is always a plus! As soon as it was assembled, I was excited to give it a try. I am 5'2 and my husband is 6'. The seat adjusts pretty easily and without much effort. We didn't have any trouble transitioning at all. It does take a little trial and error finding your "sweet spot", but I think that that would be the case with any bike. The seat and backing are comfortable and support you well. After a few minutes of using the bike, it felt great (unlike traditional bikes in my opinion). I really like the information that is displayed on the screen: time, speed, distance, calories, and pulse (the monitors are on the two side bars). You can choose to have it focus on one aspect or cycle between them. Personally, I like for it to move through them. The monitor turns on and off by itself which is nice as well. You can choose between 8 levels that adjust the tension. At first, I did not notice much of a difference, but after a few minutes you can definitely feel it!

Ultimately, I think that this was a great purchase. It's easy to use and a more comfortable way to transition into exercising more often. Now I have only had it for a day, so these are just my initial thoughts and opinions. I would like to use it for a week or two and then I can update my review!

I had the opportunity to purchase this item at a discount in exchange for an honest, unbiased review.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness Magnetic Recumbent Exercise Bike with Silent Belt Drive, Performance Monitor, BMI and Body Fat Calculator, 275 LB Max Weight - SF-RB4953

text_fidelity_a:
GOOGO Camping Pop Up Tent 4 Person, Instant Family Automatic Tent with 4 Mesh Windows, UPF 50+ UV Protection, Easy Set Up&Take Down, Waterproof Windproof Tent for Camping Hiking Backpacking Backyard Let me preface my review by saying that I absolutely HATE tent camping. However, there are places in the Big Bend region of Texas that you can only access by horseback or on foot. And that requires tent camping. I ride.

After 4 nights in the northern most reaches of Big Bend Ranch State Park, using this tent, I have not revised my opinion of tent camping in general. I made base camp in a remote, long unused old ranch camp which offered a covered 2 sided shed to put the tent under. It was 103 on day 2, so shade is critical. Rain wasn't a concern at all, so I cannot speak to the tent's ability to stay dry inside or not.

It is perfectly capable of staying stupid hot though. The window covers don't roll up properly or stay up when you manage to finagle them up. So any breeze passing by, passes you by.

Additionally, the hook at the center top for a fan or lantern was already coming unstitched the first night. Fortunately, I was sleeping outside where it was cooler when the lantern fell.

Those two issues aside, the tent weighs very little. It pops up and is fully supported in a minute with little effort at all. Taking it down on day 5 was equally simple. It's not really a 3 person tent unless you're tiny people who really like to snuggle.
text_fidelity_b: GOOGO Camping Pop Up Tent 4 Person, Instant Family Automatic Tent with 4 Mesh Windows, UPF 50+ UV Protection, Easy Set Up&Take Down, Waterproof Windproof Tent for Camping Hiking Backpacking Backyard

Coleman OneSource Rechargeable Camping System I still have and use my father's original Coleman gas lantern that we took to our deer shack every year in upper Wisconsin. That would make it about 65 years old! We've even used it here in Florida when power goes out because of hurricanes and severe storms.

That being said I wouldn't pay $59.99 for this particular LED lantern. While it is a well-made and effective product it is out- priced and out-performed by many alternative products of its type. The only way it might make some sense is if you subscribed to Coleman's theory of a "OneSource" rechargeable camping system and purchased most or all of its components.

That would be a similar strategy to me buying all DeWalt 20V battery tools in order to use the same batteries and chargers for all of my cordless tools. Now that has worked out extremely well for me. But camping is not even on our "to do" list. My wife's idea of camping would be to stay in a motel without all the usual amenities.

Etekcity Water Filter Straw Camping Water Purification Portable Water Filter Survival Kit for Camping, Hiking, Hurricanes I've had this on my bug-out list for a while now. At last I got it. I had questions I had doubts, because I was at first thinking of this as a filtration system. Yes it filtrates water.... no it is not a general filtration system. It is a "Personal" filter. A sip straw with advantages. Emphasis on the 'sip'. If you got as far as the comments section, you've seen what they say about it. This is for hiking, rather than camping use. Something to get water from point A to your mouth. However.... I did want to find out if I could use the bag to filter water into a cup for heating and it DOES work! You fill the bag with water... as clear as you can find, screw it into the straw, and gently but firmly squeeze. Filtered water will slowly dribble out of the sipping end. Not fast, but if you need a cup of coffee or some soup, it would be worth it. We are not talking kitchen magic here folks, we are talking survival.
To make this last as long as possible, use the clearest water you can find, use the little blue add-on filter, and backwash every time you use it. Just remember, water from a street gutter is not a good source, because of all the chemical contaminates that might be in it. This is for dirt, microbes, and insect contamination, not oil, anti-freeze and cleaners!
Picture 1 shows the bag screwed into the base, 2 shows the long folded tube attached to the base. you can also take off the short tube from the blue filter and attach it to the end of the long tube. Picture 3 shows the blue filter and the disk replacement filters for it (you get 6 total), and 4 shows the back-flow set-up. The plunger tube snugs 'into' not 'over' the mouth piece and the small blue filter's tube as well.

This was one of the Eteckcity products that I could get free or at reduced price in exchange for a review. I won't 'guess' if it works I won't say something I don't believe. This my honest opinion of a product I acquired to use personally.
text_fidelity_b: Etekcity Water Filter Straw Camping Water Purification Portable Water Filter Survival Kit for Camping, Hiking, Hurricanes

text_fidelity_a:
Optimus Crux Lite with Tera Solo Cook Set Received it today in preparation for an upcoming trip, so this is coming from one use - lunch time.

Upon opening, the pots and pans are tiny! If you're a large hungry man, you'll need a bigger set unless you just plan on boiling water for dehydrated meals. Handles seem strong enough to lift as much that fits without bending. Pot has 8, 12, 16 ounce markings readable from the inside. Then pan/lid combo is nice, however I'd like to see the pot go up to 24 ounces, with a shallower pan lid. It seems just slightly too deep for a pan.

The stove is a jet burner. It oxidized after the first use, but I didn't buy it for looks so whatever. It puts out a ton of heat. I really like the wide burner instead of a narrow one to prevent hot spots. On a simmer, the flame will heat the entire bottom of this pot set, awesome!

Trial run: couscous with a few fresh veggies mixed in. Put 4 oz of water in to boil for the couscous on my deck. Started the stove, ran inside to grab a spoon to stir with and it was boiling by the time I got back. Great! Moved the pot aside to let it simmer a bit with the couscous in (3 oz). Mixed in a few (5) cherry tomatoes, some carrot slices, a little bit of white onion, a little garlic and a teaspoon of olive oil into the little pan lid. Put that on and stirred that around for a few minutes. Rotated back to the couscous and then the veggies again one more time. Mixed it all together for a decent sized lunch. Not super filling, but plenty. Could have added plenty more couscous if I was hungrier.

What I didn't like:

The pot and pan cooled almost immediately. Great for cleanup, not so great when you're cooking in both.

The valve control is touchy. Everyone said this about this stove but the problem is not the valve, but the foldout control. As you turn it, if it bends in or out, the gas can turn up or down. With a little practice and focus, it can easily simmer on a low setting.

All in all, I feel like this is a decent set. Should last for plenty of trips where you don't need to cook for anyone else.
text_fidelity_b: Optimus Crux Lite with Tera Solo Cook Set

text_fidelity_a:
Horizon Fitness T101 Treadmill I researched the hell out of treadmill before buying this one looking at costco, sams club, amazon, sears, etc and reading product reviews all over the internet. What sold me on this the most was the east of assembly and the sturdyness. My husband is 6'-2 and 300lbs. This has a 300lb deck and we have had no problems. Also what this offered over other models in the same class was 2" more of deck, a beafier motor and longer warrranty...all big pluses when you live in a rural area. A pleasant surprise on this model that wasnt listed was a cooling fan feature with three settings to at least move the air around your face when you get that heart pumping and a little sweat rolling down.
This is a fold up model, but I would like it more if folded up a full 90 degrees, but even at an angle, this has one of the highest angles that I've seen, folding at about at 65-70 degree angle...very much out of the way.
The thing is loaded with features, one which is nice is a VERY slow speed....1/2 mph...which for my extended family, is what my sneior father recovering from his second round of CHF needs. He know he needs to walk and has tried other friends treadmills, but they don't go slow enough...usually only .7 of .8 mph. The .5 mph in his exhaustive, delicate state is perfect to start and move him up to .7 and .8 mph for 5-6 minutes. Doesn't sound like much, but when your old and recovering, its alot. He's already seen an improvement in his endurance. On the other end of the spectrum, I like to move that incline all the way up to 10% and move out at 3 mph for 20 minutes (this is when the fan feels really nice, as does being able to plug in your ipod or mp3 player) and then back down to 2-3% grade for 10-15 minute cool down. Even my daughter is liking a treadmill.
I took us about 35-40 minutes to assemble...including unpacking from the box.
Delivery was great, though, because I am rural, I package actually arrived in Reno from the shipper within a few days, but then I had to way 3 weeks for the "truck" to have "a load" to head out into the rural areas for a delivery run. But when it did arrive, the driver moved it right into the garage for us (which sits 150 feet from the street). So 5 stars for the driver.
I can't really find anything that this treadmill doesn't do. I tend to buy things that fall somewhere in the middle when it comes to customer reviews, but a few things...like appliances, TVs and this treadmill, I wanted to get as much bang for my buck as I could. Yes, I would love to have the money to buy a Solei or other high end model, but for my family needs, my budget, the durability that it must stand up to, I am extremely pleased.
text_fidelity_b: Horizon Fitness T101 Treadmill

text_fidelity_a: CamelBak Eddy Kids Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Bottle 12 oz,  Stainless My husband and I have used Camelbak bottles for over 15 years, and we both still use our insulated stainless bottles that are 9 years old. Our kids have been using the camelbak kids bottles for the past 2 years, and while I don’t believe a perfect kids water bottle exists, these are my favorite option. The main problem I’ve seen with camelbak kids bottles is that my 2 and 3 year old chew on the bite valve, which cause it to split wider than it should, then drip when the valve is open and it’s laying on its side. I have probably purchased 8 replacement bite valves for their bottles in the past 2 years because they only seem to last us 6 months or so before the leaking gets out of control. Thankfully Amazon sells 4 packs of replacement valves. If your kid is older and doesn’t chew on it as much, or even if they shut the valve after taking a drink, then that shouldn’t be an issue. Overall I like the camelbak design and I can clean it really well using a bottle brush and straw cleaner. As far as this stainless option goes, it is obviously more prone to being dented and banged up. We already have a nice gouge in the side after being dropped from 2 feet on to tile. But it will keep drinks cold for pretty much the whole day if you give it a few cubes of ice, and there won’t be condensation on the bottle. I love that I can put ice in this and not worry about it making a condensation puddle on my coffee table! I will happily take the dents in exchange for cold water all day long.
